task: Build Sports v1, the fourth minigame of the esl-likes 3D ESL game, as a complete playable slice: a 3D playground with a central plaza and four sport zones; the child asks waiting NPCs 'What sport do you like?', hears 'I like ___.', leads the followers across the field, and each follower joins in at their zone with a procedural sport animation; levels, wrong-zone handling, listen-again, scoring and the turnaround. The shared shell, speech stack, Restaurant, Coloring and Drink Stand already exist and work; this order adds one minigame against the frozen interface.
requirements: Read SPEC.md first: the anti-shortcut rule near the top, section 3 ('Listening again'), and section 7 (Sports v1), which is the frozen design and wins over any assumption. Read DESIGN_DECISIONS.md for existing rationale (especially the 2026-09-12 Sports entry). Do not modify SPEC.md.

Create src/minigames/sports/ with at least index.js (createSports(ctx) controller), scoring.js (PURE logic, no DOM, no three.js) and scoring.test.mjs (node:test). Further modules in that folder are welcome (field building, follower logic, sport animations).

createSports(ctx) implements the frozen interface { id, enter(level), update(dt), exit() } exactly as src/minigames/restaurant/index.js does, including the same level resolution (enter(level) falling back to settings 'difficulty', clamped 1..3) and the settings subscription for micFree / textSize.

Register it: src/main.js minigames map gets ['sports', createSports]; in src/config/lesson.js set the sports lesson available: true and add a UI.sports block with ALL new Japanese strings (including the wrong-zone line from SPEC 7). No UI text hardcoded elsewhere. NPC answers come only from answerFor(LESSON, sportId).

Field per SPEC 7: central plaza; four zones in the four corners, each identifiable from across the field by silhouette and colour (goal + green pitch, hoop + orange court, backstop + brown diamond, net + sand) plus a large sign with a picture and the English word (readable at 1366x768, as the Drink Stand signs now are). A clear straight path from the plaza to each zone that does not cross any other zone. Crossing the field takes a few seconds. Zone-to-corner assignment shuffled once per session via a pure seedable function in scoring.js.

Controls and camera as in the Restaurant: WASD/arrows with its movement feel (copy updateMovement: heading atan2(move.x, -move.y), shortest-way turning), follow camera from a raised three-quarter angle keeping the avatar and followers in view; generous proximity to talk to a waiting NPC via promptQuestion(ctx, LESSON, { isActive, onAccepted }) from src/systems/speechPrompt.js. No mouse-look, no pointer lock, no manual camera rotation.

Loop per SPEC 7: NPCs wait at random plaza spots; asked -> answer via ctx.dialogue with answerFor(LESSON, sport) (spoken + bubble), bubble then disappears; no ticket, icon or persistent text of the answer anywhere. The NPC then follows; multiple followers trail in a line behind the avatar without clipping through each other or the avatar. Entering a zone area: every follower whose sport matches walks into the zone and plays there for the rest of the session with a procedural looping sport animation and a moving ball (soccer kick at the goal, basketball shot at the hoop, baseball bat swing, volleyball pass over the net); emote-yes and a happy Japanese line. Entering a zone where NO follower matches: followers shake their heads (procedural head/body shake), a Japanese bubble with NO English repeat, and they keep following. A zone visit is counted once per entry (leaving and re-entering counts again); walking along the paths never counts.

Listening again (SPEC 3): the shared createListenAgain({ root, label: UI.listenAgain, onPress }) from src/ui/listenAgain.js is visible while anyone is following; pressing it replays each current follower's exact answer sentence in turn (bubble over each) and marks each of them replayed. Never on Space, never deducts normal credit.

Difficulty per SPEC 7: L1 3 NPCs one at a time (the next appears on the plaza after a delivery); L2 4 NPCs in two waves of two; L3 6 NPCs in two waves of three. No timer, no patience meter, no failure state.

Anti-shortcut per SPEC 7: each NPC's sport uniformly random over all four, independent of model, spot, asking order and other NPCs; repeats allowed (pure seedable pickSport(rng)). NPCs carry no ball or kit; nothing on an NPC or in the scene hints at their zone; waiting spots random.
NPC models: any Kenney key except characters.playerModel ('a'), random per NPC; do NOT tint textured Kenney models. Kenney models face +z at rotation.y = 0.

Scoring in scoring.js: pure scoreSession(records) where each record is { outcome: 'first' | 'later', replayed: boolean }. 'first' = joined without any wrong-zone visit while that NPC was following; 'later' = one or more wrong-zone visits happened while it was following. Points: first 5, later 2; +1 memory bonus if never replayed. ratio = earned / (6 * count). Stars: >= 0.75 -> 3, >= 0.4 -> 2, else 1; first-try share < 0.5 can never give 3 stars. The controller records a wrong-zone visit against EVERY NPC following at that moment.

scoring.test.mjs must cover at least: all first-try, no replays -> 3 stars; all first-try, every NPC replayed -> still 3 stars; a seeded touring simulation (one follower at a time, visiting zones in a random order until it joins) reaches 3 stars in under 1% of sessions; first-try share below half never gives 3 stars; pickSport over several hundred seeded draws covers all four; the zone shuffle is a permutation.

Turnaround after the last NPC joins: an NPC (e.g. the last one delivered walking back to the avatar, or a coach at the plaza) asks via promptAnswer(ctx, LESSON, ...) with all four sports, framed as a grounded readable two-shot, reacts warmly (e.g. the avatar joins that sport's zone for a moment), then finish({ stars, detail: { category: 'sport', answer } }).

Test hooks: stable DOM class names for the minigame's own overlay (at least an instruction element and a notice element), and a READ-ONLY window.__eslDebug.sports getter returning { phase, level, player: { x, z }, zones: [{ id, x, z }], npcs: [{ state, asked, x, z }] } where state is one of 'hidden' | 'waiting' | 'following' | 'joined' and x/z are world coordinates (W moves the avatar toward -z, D toward +x). It must NOT expose NPCs' wanted sports. Remove it in exit().

exit() disposes every owned geometry, material, texture and canvas, removes overlays, listeners, injected styles and the debug hook, and clears speech/hud targets, exactly as the Restaurant does. Entering Sports twice from the hub must not leak or duplicate anything.

npm test and npm run build must both pass. Capture your own 1366x768 screenshots of: the field on entry, an NPC answering, two followers trailing, an NPC playing in its zone, the wrong-zone head shake, and the turnaround; state what you checked in them.
constraints: Do NOT modify SPEC.md, src/systems/*, src/ui/*, src/scenes/hub.js, src/styles.css, scripts/, the Restaurant, Coloring, Drink Stand or the placeholder. If a shared system genuinely lacks something, say so in the summary instead of editing it. The only shared edits allowed: the registry line and import in src/main.js, and in src/config/lesson.js the sports `available` flag plus a new UI.sports block.
Do NOT add dependencies. three and vite only.
Do NOT build Zoo, a universal minigame base class, or shared scoring maths with other minigames.

Source-edit hygiene: edit files with structured file tools. If a shell-based edit fails on quoting or escaping, stop editing through the shell for that change and use the file tools; never escalate through nested shell/python/regex patches.
Do not inline code into shell commands; run the declared npm scripts.
notes: Governing rule (SPEC): the NPC's English answer must be information the child needs. For Sports: a child who ignores 'I like soccer.' can still finish by touring zones (never stuck) but can never reliably get three stars. In your summary, state how each anti-shortcut leak in SPEC was checked (fixed mapping, order, elimination, colour/appearance cues, default selection, free trial-and-error). Tone: the active, bouncy stage between the fast Drink Stand and the exploratory Zoo; the followers trailing the avatar and bursting into play at their zone is the fun. Lessons from the Drink Stand review, apply them up front: characters and their answer bubbles must be clearly visible and never hidden behind scenery or the avatar; waiting NPCs must never block anything; signs must be large and readable; any character asking the turnaround must stand on a real floor. Known traps: Kenney models face +z; one avatar key; tinting textured Kenney models turns skin grey; the dialogue bubble uses width max-content; focused buttons must not swallow movement keys (handled in input.js). Restaurant is the reference for movement, follow camera, proximity talk and exit() hygiene; Drink Stand for signs, listen-again targeting and the debug hook; Coloring and Drink Stand for the turnaround two-shot. Append meaningful design decisions to DESIGN_DECISIONS.md as dated entries. List every file you touched.
